Moncure Daniel Conway, an American minister turned freethinker, traveled through Asia to meet the religious teachers of his age. His 1906 book, My Pilgrimage to the Wise Men of the East, tells that journey.

Conway sat with Hindu teachers, Buddhist monks, and other sages, and wrote down what they said and how they lived. He had left orthodox preaching behind, so he listened as a seeker rather than a missionary. The book became a classic of comparative religion travel writing, prized for its open mind and clear portraits of faiths then little known in America.
